newsitem.title: FINLAND: Rauma welcomes UPM move to cut stake in it.
newsitem.headline: Rauma welcomes UPM move to cut stake in it.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Rauma Oy on Tuesday welcomed its parent UPM-Kymmene Oy's decision to reduce its holding in it, expecting the move to boost the liquidity and status of Rauma shares.

"There has been no liquidity in Rauma...but now it will increase significantly," Rauma CEO Heikki Hakala told a news conference, adding that trade in Rauma shares had been particularly thin on the New York Stock Exchange.
Forestry group UPM-Kymmene said earlier that it would pay part of its 1996 dividend in Rauma shares. This would reduce UPM's holding to 59.9 percent from the current 73.3 percent.
UPM also said it intended to cut its Rauma stake further to below 50 percent.
"(That) will expand Rauma's ownership base and clarify Rauma's role as a listed company," Hakala said.
Rauma earlier reported a 679 million markka profit after financial items for 1996, up from 671 million in 1995.
